chunks: He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan reported to me from his father, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahboob, from Malik ibn Atiyyah, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, who said: Ali ibn al-Husayn Zayn al-Abidin, peace be upon them both, used to say:

"O son of Adam, you will always remain upon good so long as you have an admonisher from within yourself, and so long as self-reckoning is among your concerns, and so long as fear is your inner garment and grief your outer cloak. Indeed you shall die, be resurrected, and be made to stand before Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, [so prepare an answer]."
And may Allah bless our master Muhammad, the Prophet, and his family, and grant them abundant peace.

key_terms.المحاسبة: self-reckoning — the practice of holding oneself accountable for one's deeds
key_terms.دثارا: outer garment (dithar) — the cloak or wrap worn over other clothes, metaphor for an ever-visible quality
key_terms.شعارا: inner garment (shi'ar) — underclothing worn next to the skin, metaphor for an intimate, constant companion
key_terms.مبعوث: resurrected — raised from the dead on the Day of Judgment
key_terms.واعظ: admonisher — one who warns or counsels, here referring to the inner voice of conscience

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Zayn al-Abidin say about self-accountability and preparing for the afterlife?
ai.summary: Imam Zayn al-Abidin (the Fourth Imam) offers a profound exhortation to humanity using the address "O son of Adam." He identifies four conditions that keep a person on the right path: an inner conscience that admonishes, habitual self-reckoning, the fear of God worn close to the heart like an undergarment, and sorrowful awareness of one's shortcomings worn visibly like an outer cloak. He then reminds the listener of death, resurrection, and standing before God, urging preparation of one's answer.
